model.name: Incident Response
model.purpose: Provide the format-neutral context an agent needs to open, operate, inspect and close an incident response engagement from detection through containment, recovery coordination and lessons learned.
model.scope_statement: This model is the response-process record: a case aggregate binding a declared incident to a mandated response capability, its triage and containment decisions, authorised actions, evidence and communication records, closure and learning outcomes. It owns the response case, not the incident entity, not the continuity or recovery plan, and not the runtime systems that execute or enforce actions. Evidence is drawn primarily from cybersecurity incident management sources; an adopting Dimension may bind a non-cyber incident model to the same case structure.
in_scope: Response capability mandate, constituency, authority level and decision rights as applied to a case
Binding of a governing playbook, plan or procedure version to a case, and recorded deviations from it
Case identity, alternative identifiers held by cooperating teams, and the case scope perimeter
Triage decision record, assigned response tier and response-side clocks
Detection and report intake, discovery source, and the event-to-incident declaration decision
Analysis findings, hypotheses, confidence and response-side impact assessment
Authorisation, tracking and outcome references for containment, eradication and mitigation actions
Invocation reference and parameters for continuity or recovery plans governed by WM-ACT-043
Evidence register entries, custody handoffs at the case boundary and preservation holds
Case chronology distinguishing event, detection, report, containment, recovery and closure times
Internal escalation, situation reporting, regulatory notification submissions and affected-party communication
Handling markings and disclosure control for case-derived information
Case closure, post-incident review, improvement actions and response performance measurement
out_of_scope: Definition, categorisation, severity taxonomy and affected-asset inventory of the incident itself (WM-ACT-020)
Authoring, approval, testing, exercising and lifecycle of continuity or recovery plans, and RTO/RPO targets (WM-ACT-043)
Execution, orchestration or enforcement of response actions by security tooling, and the tooling's own audit-trail semantics
Forensic acquisition, imaging and examination methodology and expert reporting
Statutory interpretation determining which reporting regime applies, and the regulator's own case handling
Threat intelligence production, actor attribution and indicator curation
Vulnerability discovery, disclosure coordination and patch management
Risk register, risk acceptance authority and enterprise control framework ownership
Identity, access and asset master data
Crisis communications strategy, litigation, insurance claims and ransom payment or sanctions decisions
Physical execution of records disposal and platform-level retention enforcement

boundary_notes.distinction: The incident model owns what happened: incident identity, classification, severity, affected assets and impact facts. This model owns how it was handled and carries only references plus response-side decisions such as priority tier and declaration.

boundary_notes.neighbor: WM-ACT-043 Continuity and recovery plans (outgoing REFERENCE)
boundary_notes.distinction: Plan content, approval, testing and activation lifecycle stay in the target model. This model carries only the plan reference, invocation trigger, invocation parameters and the returned acknowledgement reference.
Generic activity, case and work-record scaffolding defined by the parent is inherited, not restated; only incident-response specialisation is modelled here.

Playbook execution engines, agents, targets and command execution semantics are external. This model records the authorisation, the intended effect and a reference to execution evidence, never the execution or enforcement semantics themselves.

boundary_notes.neighbor: Digital forensics and evidence examination (candidate sibling)
boundary_notes.distinction: Collection, examination, analysis and expert reporting methodology are external. This model holds register entries, integrity digests and custody handoffs at the case boundary only.

boundary_notes.neighbor: Regulatory obligation register and legal counsel
boundary_notes.distinction: Determining which regime and threshold applies is a legal determination held elsewhere. This model binds the determined obligation to the case and records submission facts and acknowledgements.
Technique, actor and indicator definitions are external catalogue content referenced by identifier and version; this model does not curate or version them.
Maturity scoring and assessment methodology are external; this model records readiness preconditions and references to assessment outcomes relied upon at case time.

sources.title: Incident Response Recommendations and Considerations for Cybersecurity Risk Management: A CSF 2.0 Community Profile (NIST SP 800-61r3)
sources.organization: National Institute of Standards and Technology
sources.relevance: Current NIST position that incident response is expressed as a CSF 2.0 Community Profile across all six Functions rather than a standalone phase lifecycle; anchors preparation, detection, response, recovery and improvement outcomes.

sources.title: RFC 7970: The Incident Object Description Exchange Format Version 2 (IODEF)
sources.relevance: Normative data model for incident case exchange: IncidentID and AlternativeID, DetectTime/StartTime/EndTime/RecoveryTime/ReportTime/GenerationTime, Discovery source enumeration, Assessment, Contact, Expectation, History, and the purpose/status/restriction attribute vocabularies.

sources.title: RFC 2350: Expectations for Computer Security Incident Response (BCP 21)
sources.relevance: Normative disclosure template for a response capability: contact information, charter, mission, constituency, sponsorship, authority, policies on incident types and level of support, disclosure and communication, services and reporting forms.

sources.title: Traffic Light Protocol (TLP) Version 2.0
sources.organization: Forum of Incident Response and Security Teams (FIRST)
sources.relevance: Handling labels TLP:RED, TLP:AMBER, TLP:AMBER+STRICT, TLP:GREEN, TLP:CLEAR with normative rules on label form, placement and source responsibility for recipient understanding.

sources.title: FIRST CSIRT Services Framework Version 2.1
sources.organization: Forum of Incident Response and Security Teams (FIRST)
sources.relevance: Service-area, service, function and sub-function decomposition; Information Security Incident Management comprises report acceptance, incident analysis, artifact and forensic evidence analysis, mitigation and recovery, incident coordination and crisis management support.

sources.title: CACAO Security Playbooks Version 2.0
sources.relevance: Machine-readable playbook identity and versioning (id, created, modified, valid_from, valid_until, revoked, derived_from), playbook_types vocabulary, agent/target/authentication definitions, data marking definitions, signatures and workflow step types; locates execution semantics outside this model.

sources.title: STIX Version 2.1 (OASIS Standard)
sources.relevance: Common object properties (id, spec_version, created, modified, created_by_ref, revoked, confidence, external_references, object_marking_refs, granular_markings), Note SDO for analyst commentary, Sighting SRO, TLP marking definitions, and a deliberately minimal Incident SDO.

sources.title: Directive (EU) 2022/2555 (NIS 2 Directive), Articles 6 and 23
sources.organization: European Parliament and Council of the European Union
sources.relevance: Definitions of incident, incident handling, near miss and significant incident; multi-stage reporting duty of 24-hour early warning, 72-hour incident notification, intermediate report on request, one-month final report or progress report, plus service-recipient notification.

sources.title: Regulation (EU) 2016/679 (GDPR), Articles 33 and 34
sources.organization: European Parliament and Council of the European Union
sources.relevance: 72-hour personal data breach notification with required content, reasoned justification for delay, processor duty to notify the controller, Article 33(5) internal breach documentation duty, and Article 34 communication to data subjects on high risk.

sources.title: Reference Incident Classification Taxonomy: Task Force Status and Way Forward
sources.relevance: Establishes a harmonised reference incident classification for CSIRTs and law enforcement, derived from the eCSIRT.net taxonomy, and the governance of its continued maintenance.

sources.title: Reference Security Incident Taxonomy (RSIT), human-readable working copy
sources.organization: TF-CSIRT Reference Security Incident Taxonomy Working Group / ENISA
sources.relevance: Concrete classification classes and incident types (abusive content, malicious code, information gathering, intrusion attempts, intrusions, availability, information content security, fraud, vulnerable, other, test) used as an external classification vocabulary.

sources.title: NIST SP 800-184: Guide for Cybersecurity Event Recovery
sources.organization: National Institute of Standards and Technology
sources.relevance: Separates recovery planning, playbook development, testing and improvement from response execution, and supplies recovery metrics; supports placing plan ownership in WM-ACT-043 while this model records invocation and verification.

sources.title: NIST SP 800-86: Guide to Integrating Forensic Techniques into Incident Response
sources.organization: National Institute of Standards and Technology
sources.relevance: Establishes forensic practice as a discipline integrated with but distinct from incident response, including data integrity and the need to involve management and legal counsel; grounds the evidence boundary note.

sources.title: ISO/IEC 27035-1:2023 Information technology - Information security incident management - Part 1: Principles and process
sources.relevance: International phase-based incident management process (plan and prepare, detect and report, assess and decide, respond, learn lessons) and the event/incident distinction; cited at catalogue level because the normative text is paywalled and was not machine-verified in this session.

sources.title: MITRE ATT&CK Versions of ATT&CK
sources.relevance: Versioned technique catalogue with major.minor release semantics and archived versions; requires that technique references carry a catalogue version to remain resolvable.

sources.title: SIM3: Security Incident Management Maturity Model
sources.relevance: Maturity parameters covering organisational, human, tools and process aspects of a response capability; supports readiness preconditions being referenced rather than re-derived at case time.

sources.title: CIRCIA, other big cyber rules expected to get finalized this fall
sources.relevance: Used only to record that the US CIRCIA implementing rule was still not final as of mid-2026, so its 72-hour incident and 24-hour ransom-payment reporting duties must be modelled as a pending, jurisdiction-specific binding rather than an active obligation.

bundles.name: Mandate, Authority and Readiness
bundles.description: Who is empowered to respond, with what authority and decision rights, and what preparedness the capability relies on when a case opens.
bundles.rationale: Response acts are only defensible if the responding capability's constituency, authority level and governing procedures are declared in advance; RFC 2350 makes this a publication duty and the CSIRT Services Framework decomposes the services offered.

layers.name: Response Mandate and Authority
layers.description: The declared charter, constituency, service scope and the decision rights exercised during a case.

findings.name: Response capability charter and constituency
findings.description: The published mandate of the responding capability: mission, constituency, sponsorship, authority level over constituent systems, supported incident types and level of support.

questions.text: What authority does the responding capability hold over constituent systems, and is it advisory, shared or full?
answer_data: Escalation path when authority is insufficient

questions.text: Which constituency, sites and organisational units does this capability serve?
Which incident types are supported and at what declared level of support?
Which published version of the service description governs this case, and when was it last updated?

data_elements.name: Responding capability identifier
data_elements.description: Authoritative identifier of the team or capability accepting the case.

data_elements.name: Authority level
data_elements.description: Declared authority over constituent systems, from advisory through full.

data_elements.name: Constituency scope
data_elements.description: Definition of the served constituency and its stated exclusions.

data_elements.name: Service catalogue reference
data_elements.description: Reference to the services and functions the capability offers for this incident type.

artifacts.name: Response capability service description
artifacts.description: Published document following the RFC 2350 template covering contact information, charter, policies, services, reporting forms and disclaimers.
artifacts.identity_strategy: Stable resource identifier for the published description plus an explicit version label; never identified by publication date alone.

findings.name: Case roles and decision rights
findings.description: Named roles engaged on the case, their delegated decision rights, handover points and the escalation trigger to crisis management.

questions.text: Who holds the decision right for containment actions that disrupt production services?
How is case ownership handed over between shifts or teams without losing accountability?
Which condition escalates the case from response coordination into crisis management support?
How are conflicts between response, legal and business owners recorded and resolved?

data_elements.name: Case role assignment
data_elements.description: Binding of a role to an identity reference for a stated period of the case.

data_elements.name: Decision right
data_elements.description: The class of decision a role may take without further approval.

data_elements.name: Ownership handover
data_elements.description: Record of transfer of case ownership between role holders.

findings.inline_only_rationale: Role engagement is reference data: it points to identity records and duty rosters mastered elsewhere and exists only as fields on the case record, so no separately transmissible artifact is produced or needed.

layers.name: Preparedness Baseline
layers.description: Which governing procedure version and which readiness preconditions the case relies on.

findings.name: Governing playbook and procedure binding
findings.description: The identity, version and validity window of the playbook, procedure or plan invoked to govern the case, plus whether the case runs ad hoc.

questions.text: Which playbook or procedure version governs this case, and is it still within its validity window?
What playbook type applies, such as detection, investigation, mitigation or remediation?
If no playbook exists for this situation, what is recorded in its place?
How is the bound playbook version verified as unaltered at the moment of binding?

data_elements.name: Playbook reference
data_elements.description: Identifier of the externally governed playbook or procedure bound to the case.

data_elements.name: Playbook version marker
data_elements.description: Version or modification marker of the bound playbook at binding time.

data_elements.name: Playbook validity window
data_elements.description: Earliest and latest time the bound playbook is declared valid for execution.

data_elements.name: Ad hoc response flag
data_elements.description: Indicates the case proceeds without a pre-approved playbook.

findings.inline_only_rationale: The playbook itself is an externally governed object with its own identity, versioning, signatures and execution engine; this finding carries only the binding tuple of reference, version, validity and digest, which is inline reference data on the case.

findings.name: Readiness preconditions relied upon
findings.description: The readiness state the case depends on: reachable contacts, available tooling access, current training and exercise evidence, referenced rather than re-assessed.

questions.text: Which readiness preconditions must hold before this response tier can be operated?
What external assessment or exercise evidence is relied upon, and when was it produced?
Which readiness gaps were known and accepted at the time the case opened?
Are out-of-band contact and authentication means available if primary channels are compromised?

data_elements.name: Readiness precondition
data_elements.description: A named condition required before the response tier is operable.

data_elements.name: Readiness assessment reference
data_elements.description: Pointer to an externally held maturity, training or exercise record.

data_elements.name: Out-of-band channel reference
data_elements.description: Reference to the secure alternate communication and authentication means.

findings.inline_only_rationale: Maturity assessments, training records and exercise reports are produced and versioned by other programmes; this finding holds only pointers and the accepted-gap statement, so declaring a local artifact would duplicate externally mastered records.

bundles.name: Case Identity, Scope and Triage
bundles.description: How the response case is identified, bounded and prioritised, and how it binds to external classification vocabularies.
bundles.rationale: IODEF requires a tracking identifier assigned by the generating team plus alternative identifiers from cooperating teams, and separates classification vocabularies from the case record itself.

layers.name: Case Identification and Scope
layers.description: The identifiers, cross-references and perimeter that define which response engagement this is.

findings.name: Response case identity, cross-references and perimeter
findings.description: The authoritative case identifier, identifiers held by cooperating parties, the reference to the incident record handled, and the declared perimeter of the engagement.

questions.text: What is the authoritative identifier of this response case and which system issued it?
Which tracking numbers do cooperating teams, vendors or authorities use for the same engagement?
Which incident record does this case handle, and is the link one-to-one?
What is inside the response perimeter and what was explicitly excluded from it?
How are duplicate or related cases merged, split or superseded without losing identifiers?

data_elements.name: Case identifier
data_elements.description: Tracking identifier assigned by the responding capability within its own namespace.

data_elements.name: Alternative case identifier
data_elements.description: Identifier used by another team or authority for the same engagement.

data_elements.name: Handled incident reference
data_elements.description: Reference to the incident record whose facts are mastered by the incident model.

data_elements.name: Related activity reference
data_elements.description: Reference to related cases, campaigns or prior engagements.

data_elements.name: Response perimeter
data_elements.description: Declared set of in-scope and out-of-scope entities, sites or tenants for the engagement.

artifacts.name: Response case record
artifacts.description: The aggregate root record of the engagement carrying identity, cross-references, perimeter, decisions and state.
artifacts.identity_strategy: Master case-management identifier where one exists, otherwise a governed identifier within the issuing team namespace; serial numbering is monotonic within that namespace and carries no date component.

layers.name: Triage and Classification Binding
layers.description: The response-side prioritisation decision and the bindings to external classification vocabularies.

findings.name: Triage decision and response tier
findings.description: The recorded decision assigning a response tier, target response clocks and resourcing, together with the criteria version applied.

questions.text: What response tier was assigned, by whom, and against which criteria version?
Which response clocks start on triage and what are their targets?
Under what conditions is the response tier re-evaluated during the case?
How does the assigned response tier relate to the severity held on the incident record?

data_elements.name: Response tier
data_elements.description: Response-side priority class driving resourcing and clocks.

data_elements.name: Triage criteria version
data_elements.description: Version identifier of the prioritisation criteria applied.

data_elements.name: Response clock
data_elements.description: A named target interval with its start time and target duration.

data_elements.name: Triage decider reference
data_elements.description: Reference to the role or identity that assigned the tier.

findings.inline_only_rationale: Triage output is a small decision tuple stored on the case record and consumed by workflow; severity and impact facts belong to the incident model, so a separate transmissible artifact would fragment the decision from the case state it governs.

findings.name: External classification and technique bindings
findings.description: Bindings from the case to external vocabularies for incident class, adversary technique and exchange-format attributes, always with catalogue version.

questions.text: Which external classification class and type were assigned, from which taxonomy version?
Which adversary techniques are referenced and against which catalogue version?
What is the declared purpose of documenting this case for exchange, such as mitigation, reporting or traceback?
How are bindings revalidated when an external catalogue publishes a new version?

data_elements.name: Taxonomy binding
data_elements.description: Class and type value drawn from an external incident taxonomy with its version.

data_elements.name: Technique reference
data_elements.description: Versioned identifier of an adversary technique asserted for the case.

data_elements.name: Exchange purpose
data_elements.description: Declared reason the case is documented for exchange.

findings.inline_only_rationale: These are alignment bindings to catalogues owned by other organisations; the model stores only coded values, catalogue versions and confidence, and must not restate or fork the external vocabularies as local artifacts.

bundles.name: Detection Intake and Analysis
bundles.description: How the engagement was triggered, how an event became a declared incident, and what the analysis concluded for response purposes.
bundles.rationale: IODEF enumerates discovery sources and separates detection from report and generation times; the CSIRT Services Framework separates report acceptance from incident analysis; ISO/IEC 27035-1 separates events from incidents.

layers.name: Detection and Report Intake
layers.description: Receipt of the trigger and the decision that promotes it to a handled incident.

findings.name: Detection and report intake
findings.description: How the engagement was triggered: discovery source, reporting party, channel, submitted content and receipt acknowledgement.

questions.text: By which discovery source was the situation first noticed, such as monitoring, audit, external notification or law enforcement?
Who reported the situation and how was the reporting party authenticated?
What acknowledgement was returned to the reporter and within what interval?
How complete and reliable was the initial report, and what was missing?

data_elements.name: Discovery source
data_elements.description: Coded means by which the situation was discovered.

data_elements.name: Reporting party contact
data_elements.description: Contact reference for the party that submitted the report.

data_elements.name: Report receipt time
data_elements.description: Time the report was received by the responding capability.

data_elements.name: Intake completeness assessment
data_elements.description: Assessment of whether the submitted report met the minimum reporting form.

artifacts.name: Inbound incident report
artifacts.description: The submitted report as received, whether a reporting form, structured exchange document or transcribed notification.
artifacts.identity_strategy: Submission identifier assigned on receipt, bound to the case identifier; the original sender reference is retained as provenance rather than as identity.

findings.name: Event to incident declaration
findings.description: The decision that promotes one or more events to a declared incident under response, including the declaring authority and the basis.

questions.text: Who declared the incident and under which delegated authority?
On what basis was the event judged to be an incident rather than a near miss or false positive?
How is a declaration reversed if analysis later shows no incident occurred?
Is a near miss recorded even when no incident is declared, and where?

data_elements.name: Declaration state
data_elements.description: Whether the trigger stands as an event, near miss, declared incident or rejected report.

data_elements.name: Declaration time
data_elements.description: Time the incident was formally declared under response.

data_elements.name: Declaration basis
data_elements.description: Stated reasoning and evidence references supporting the declaration.

findings.inline_only_rationale: Declaration is a state transition with an authority reference and a basis statement recorded on the case record; the incident entity it promotes is mastered by the composing incident model, so no independent document is created here.

layers.name: Investigation and Analysis
layers.description: Analytical conclusions and the response-side impact assessment that drive containment and notification decisions.

findings.name: Analysis findings, hypotheses and confidence
findings.description: Working hypotheses, supporting and contradicting observations, confidence, and the root cause status as understood during response.

questions.text: What hypotheses about the attack path are open, and what would falsify each one?
What confidence is attached to each conclusion and on what scale?
Has a root cause been established, and is it provisional or confirmed?
Which observations underpin a finding and where are the underlying data held?

data_elements.name: Analysis hypothesis
data_elements.description: A stated hypothesis with its current status.

data_elements.name: Analysis confidence
data_elements.description: Confidence assigned to a stated conclusion on a declared scale.

data_elements.name: Root cause status
data_elements.description: Whether root cause is unknown, provisional or confirmed.

artifacts.name: Investigation analysis note
artifacts.description: Dated analytical note attached to the case or to referenced objects, carrying assessment, confidence and author, without altering the referenced objects.
artifacts.identity_strategy: Governed object identifier assigned by the analysis platform, with author reference and creation and modification markers; sequence within a case is derived from those markers, not from the identifier.

findings.name: Response-side impact assessment
findings.description: The assessed impact used to drive response decisions and notification thresholds, distinguished from the incident model's authoritative impact facts.

questions.text: Which impact categories are assessed for response purposes and on what scale?
What is the current estimate of affected parties or records, and how uncertain is it?
Does the assessed impact cross a reporting or escalation threshold, and which one?
Is cross-border or multi-jurisdiction impact likely, and on what basis?

data_elements.name: Impact assessment entry
data_elements.description: Assessed impact in a named category on a declared scale at a stated time.

data_elements.name: Affected party estimate
data_elements.description: Approximate number of affected data subjects, records or services.

data_elements.name: Affected jurisdiction reference
data_elements.description: Jurisdictions in which impact is assessed as likely.

findings.inline_only_rationale: This is a working assessment that changes repeatedly during a case and exists to drive response and notification decisions; the authoritative impact statement belongs to the incident model, so publishing a separate local artifact would create a competing record of fact.

bundles.name: Response Actions and Recovery Coordination
bundles.description: Authorisation and tracking of response actions, deviations from the governing playbook, and the coordination interface to continuity and recovery plans.
bundles.rationale: CACAO locates command execution in agents and engines outside the case record, SP 800-184 separates recovery planning and execution from response, and the CSIRT Services Framework treats mitigation and recovery as coordinated services.

layers.name: Action Authorisation and Tracking
layers.description: What was authorised, by whom, with what intended effect and what recorded outcome reference.

findings.name: Response action authorisation and outcome reference
findings.description: Each authorised containment, eradication or mitigation action with its target reference, approver, requested and completed times and a reference to execution evidence held by the executing system.

questions.text: Which action was authorised, against which target, and who approved it?
What effect was the action intended to achieve and how would success be recognised?
Where is the evidence that the action was carried out, and who holds it?
Is the action reversible, and what is the rollback path if it causes harm?

data_elements.name: Action record identifier
data_elements.description: Identifier of the authorised action within the case.

data_elements.name: Action target reference
data_elements.description: Reference to the asset, account or network object the action addresses.

data_elements.name: Action authorisation
data_elements.description: Approver reference, authorisation basis and authorisation time.

data_elements.name: Execution evidence reference
data_elements.description: Pointer to the executing system's record that the action was performed.

data_elements.name: Action request time
data_elements.description: Time the action was requested or authorised.

artifacts.name: Response action task record
artifacts.description: Case-scoped record of one authorised action carrying target, authorisation, intended effect, timing and outcome references.
artifacts.identity_strategy: Master work-management identifier where the adopting Dimension operates one, otherwise a monotonic sequence within the case identifier namespace with no date component.

findings.name: Containment decisions, trade-offs and playbook deviations
findings.description: Recorded decision points where containment competed with evidence preservation or service availability, and any departure from the bound playbook.

questions.text: Which trade-off between containment speed, service availability and evidence preservation was chosen and why?
Where did the response depart from the bound playbook, and who approved the departure?
What conditions would abort or reverse the containment strategy?
Which dependencies or third parties had to consent before containment could proceed?

data_elements.name: Decision entry
data_elements.description: A recorded decision with options, choice, rationale and deciding role.

data_elements.name: Playbook deviation entry
data_elements.description: Departure from the bound playbook with justification and approver.

data_elements.name: Evidence preservation conflict flag
data_elements.description: Marks that a containment action risked destroying evidence.

artifacts.name: Decision and deviation record
artifacts.description: Reviewable record of material response decisions and departures from the governing playbook, suitable for post-incident review and external scrutiny.
artifacts.identity_strategy: Sequence within the case identifier namespace, bound to the deciding role reference and authorisation time; no date component in the identifier.

layers.name: Recovery Coordination
layers.description: The interface between the response case and externally governed continuity and recovery plans, and the response-side verification of restoration.

findings.name: Continuity and recovery plan invocation binding
findings.description: The reference, trigger, parameters and acknowledgement recorded when the response requests invocation of a continuity or recovery plan governed by another model.

questions.text: Which continuity or recovery plan version was requested, and by which reference?
What condition triggered the invocation request and who was authorised to make it?
Which case-specific parameters were passed with the invocation request?
What acknowledgement or activation reference was returned by the plan owner?

data_elements.name: Continuity or recovery plan reference
data_elements.description: Reference to the externally governed plan requested for invocation.

data_elements.name: Invocation request
data_elements.description: Trigger condition, requesting role, parameters and request time.

data_elements.name: Invocation acknowledgement reference
data_elements.description: Reference returned by the plan owner confirming receipt or activation.

findings.inline_only_rationale: This finding deliberately holds only a reference, a trigger, parameters and an acknowledgement pointer. Plan content, activation state, execution steps, testing and completion are owned by the referenced continuity and recovery model, so producing a local plan or activation artifact here would duplicate that model's lifecycle.

findings.name: Restoration verification and residual risk hand-off
findings.description: The response-side verification that response objectives were met, the heightened monitoring period, and the residual risk handed to risk owners.

questions.text: How was it verified that affected services and systems returned to an acceptable state?
When was recovery reached, as distinct from when containment was achieved?
What heightened monitoring period follows restoration and what would reopen the case?
Which residual risks remain accepted after restoration, and who accepted them?

data_elements.name: Recovery time
data_elements.description: Time at which the affected environment was assessed as recovered.

data_elements.name: Verification result
data_elements.description: Outcome of the response-side restoration verification.

data_elements.name: Heightened monitoring period
data_elements.description: Duration of post-restoration watch before the case may close.

data_elements.name: Residual risk reference
data_elements.description: Pointer to the risk record accepting any remaining exposure.

artifacts.name: Restoration verification record
artifacts.description: Record of the checks, results and sign-off used by the response to conclude that response objectives were met.
artifacts.identity_strategy: Bound to the case identifier with the verifying role reference and verification timestamp; identity derives from the case namespace, not from the verification date.

bundles.name: Evidence, Chronology and Record Integrity
bundles.description: How case-related evidence is registered and held, and how the case chronology and change history are kept trustworthy.
bundles.rationale: Forensic practice requires integrity and custody discipline while keeping examination methodology separate; IODEF distinguishes detection, start, end, recovery, report and generation times and carries an explicit history log.

layers.name: Evidence Register and Holds
layers.description: Registration, integrity and custody of evidence at the case boundary, and preservation obligations.

findings.name: Evidence register entries and custody handoffs
findings.description: Register of evidence items relied upon by the case with integrity values, acquiring party and custody transfers into and out of the response capability.

questions.text: Which evidence items does this case rely on and where is each physically or logically held?
What integrity value was recorded at acquisition and when was it last reverified?
Which custody transfers occurred, between whom, and under what authorisation?
Which handling constraints were imposed for possible legal use, and who set them?

data_elements.name: Evidence item identifier
data_elements.description: Identifier of a registered evidence item relied upon by the case.

data_elements.name: Evidence integrity value
data_elements.description: Cryptographic digest with named algorithm recorded at acquisition.

data_elements.name: Custody transfer entry
data_elements.description: Transfer of custody with parties, authorisation and time.

artifacts.name: Evidence register entry
artifacts.description: Case-boundary register entry describing an evidence item, its integrity value, custodian and handling constraints.
artifacts.identity_strategy: Master evidence-management identifier where one exists, otherwise a monotonic sequence within the case namespace bound to the acquiring party; no date component.

artifacts.name: Custody handoff receipt
artifacts.description: Signed or acknowledged receipt recording transfer of an evidence item between custodians.
artifacts.identity_strategy: Sequence within the evidence register entry namespace, bound to both party references and the transfer timestamp.

findings.name: Preservation hold and retention classification
findings.description: Holds that suspend routine disposal of case records and evidence, the retention class assigned, and the party that must execute disposal when the hold lifts.

questions.text: Which records and evidence are under preservation hold and who imposed the hold?
What retention class and minimum period apply to the case record itself?
Which case content contains personal data requiring minimisation before long-term retention?
Who authorises release of the hold and who executes the resulting disposition?

data_elements.name: Preservation hold flag
data_elements.description: Indicates whether routine disposal is suspended for case records.

data_elements.name: Retention class
data_elements.description: Retention class assigned to the case record and its attachments.

data_elements.name: Disposition owner reference
data_elements.description: Party responsible for executing disposal when the hold is released.

artifacts.name: Preservation hold notice
artifacts.description: Notice recording the scope, basis, imposing authority and release conditions of a hold over case records and evidence.
artifacts.identity_strategy: Sequence within the case namespace bound to the imposing authority reference; the effective period is carried as fields, never as part of the identifier.

layers.name: Chronology and Record Provenance
layers.description: Time semantics of the case and the history of who changed the record and on what basis.

findings.name: Case chronology, time semantics and change history
findings.description: The reconstructed sequence of the engagement with explicitly typed times, together with the log of record changes, their authors and the systems they came from.

questions.text: Which distinct time types are recorded, such as event start, detection, report, containment, recovery and record generation?
Which timestamp constitutes awareness for the purpose of starting regulatory clocks?
How are uncertain or estimated times distinguished from observed ones?
Who changed the case record, when, and what was the stated reason?
From which source system did each imported element arrive, and at what ingestion time?

data_elements.name: Event start time
data_elements.description: Time the underlying activity is assessed to have started.

data_elements.name: Detection time
data_elements.description: Time the activity was first detected.

data_elements.name: Record generation time
data_elements.description: Time this case record or exchange document was generated.

data_elements.name: Awareness time
data_elements.description: Determined moment of awareness used to start notification clocks.

data_elements.name: History entry
data_elements.description: Change log entry with author, time, description and originating system.

artifacts.name: Case chronology
artifacts.description: Ordered chronology of the engagement with typed timestamps, uncertainty markers and references to supporting entries.
artifacts.identity_strategy: Bound to the case identifier with a generation marker for each issued version; supersession is expressed by version, never by embedding a date in the identifier.

bundles.name: Communication, Notification and Sharing
bundles.description: Internal escalation and situation reporting, external and regulatory notification, affected-party communication, and control of onward disclosure.
bundles.rationale: NIS2 imposes staged reporting duties, GDPR imposes separate supervisory-authority and data-subject duties, and TLP governs how case-derived information may be shared onward.

layers.name: Internal Escalation and Situation Reporting
layers.description: Who inside the organisation was informed, when, through which channel, and at what reporting cadence.

findings.name: Internal escalation and situation reporting
findings.description: The record of internal notifications, escalation steps and periodic situation reports issued during the engagement.

questions.text: At what cadence are situation reports issued for this response tier, and to which audiences?
Which internal escalation steps were taken and what triggered each one?
Which communication channel was used, and was it out-of-band because primary systems were suspect?
Which internal audiences were deliberately not informed, and on what basis?

data_elements.name: Internal notification entry
data_elements.description: Record of an internal party informed, with channel and time.

data_elements.name: Situation report cadence
data_elements.description: Interval at which situation reports are due for the assigned tier.

data_elements.name: Communication channel reference
data_elements.description: Channel used, including any out-of-band alternative.

artifacts.name: Situation report
artifacts.description: Periodic report of current status, actions taken, next steps and outstanding decisions for a defined internal audience.
artifacts.identity_strategy: Monotonic sequence within the case identifier namespace with an audience marker; the reporting period is carried in fields, not in the identifier.

layers.name: External and Regulatory Notification
layers.description: Binding of determined reporting obligations to the case, and communication to affected parties and the public.

findings.name: Regulatory notification binding and submission record
findings.description: For each applicable regime, the bound deadline structure, the clock start, and the record of each submission and its acknowledgement, without owning the legal determination itself.

questions.text: Which reporting regimes were determined applicable, by whom, and against which case facts?
Which submission stages does the bound regime require and what is each deadline relative to the clock start?
What was submitted, to which recipient authority, and what reference was returned?
If a deadline was missed, what reasoned justification for the delay was recorded?
Which mandated content elements were included, and which were still unknown at submission?

data_elements.name: Reporting regime binding
data_elements.description: Reference to a determined applicable regime with its determining party.

data_elements.name: Submission stage
data_elements.description: Named stage such as early warning, notification, intermediate or final report.

data_elements.name: Submission deadline
data_elements.description: Absolute deadline derived from the bound regime and the clock start.

data_elements.name: Authority acknowledgement reference
data_elements.description: Reference returned by the receiving authority for a submission.

data_elements.name: Delay justification
data_elements.description: Recorded reasons where a submission was later than the deadline.

artifacts.name: Regulatory notification submission
artifacts.description: The dispatched notification for one stage of one regime, retained together with its transmission and acknowledgement references.
artifacts.identity_strategy: Sequence within the pairing of case identifier and regime binding, so that stages remain ordered; the authority's own reference is stored as an alternative identifier.

findings.name: Affected-party and public communication
findings.description: Communication to affected individuals, customers or service recipients and any public statement, including approval and the content required for recipients to protect themselves.

questions.text: What determination triggered direct communication to affected individuals rather than authority notification alone?
Which protective recommendations and contact points were given to recipients?
How were recipients reached when direct contact was disproportionate or impossible?
Who approved the wording before release and which parties reviewed it?

data_elements.name: Affected audience reference
data_elements.description: Reference to the population addressed by a communication.

data_elements.name: Protective advice
data_elements.description: Recommendations issued to recipients to mitigate adverse effects.

data_elements.name: Communication approval
data_elements.description: Approver reference and approval time for released wording.

artifacts.name: Affected-party notice
artifacts.description: Issued communication to affected individuals, customers or service recipients, retained in the released wording.
artifacts.identity_strategy: Sequence within the case namespace with an audience marker; superseding corrections reference the prior notice identifier.

layers.name: Information Sharing Controls
layers.description: Handling markings and disclosure control applied to case-derived information.

findings.name: Handling markings and onward disclosure control
findings.description: The handling label applied to case content, its mapping to exchange-format markings, and the record of onward disclosure packages and redactions.

questions.text: Which handling label applies to this case content and how is it displayed on issued material?
How does the handling label map to markings in the exchange formats used, and where does the mapping break down?
Who may share this content onward, to whom, and under what condition?
What was redacted or aggregated before onward sharing and who authorised it?

data_elements.name: Handling label
data_elements.description: Sharing label applied to case content or to a specific element.

data_elements.name: Exchange marking reference
data_elements.description: Reference to the marking object used in an exchange format.

data_elements.name: Onward disclosure entry
data_elements.description: Record of content disclosed to a named recipient with the condition applied.

artifacts.name: Marked disclosure package
artifacts.description: Case-derived material prepared for a specific recipient, carrying the handling label on the material itself and a record of any redaction.
artifacts.identity_strategy: Sequence within the case namespace bound to the recipient reference and the applied handling label; identity never encodes the disclosure date.

bundles.name: Closure, Learning and Assurance
bundles.description: How a case reaches a defensible end state, what is learned from it, and how response performance and record quality are evidenced.
bundles.rationale: IODEF carries an explicit workflow status vocabulary, ISO/IEC 27035-1 makes lessons learned a named phase, and SP 800-61r3 places improvement inside cybersecurity risk management rather than treating it as an optional postscript.

layers.name: Closure and Post-Incident Review
layers.description: The end state of the case and the structured learning drawn from it.

findings.name: Case status model and closure
findings.description: The workflow status vocabulary of the case, closure preconditions, the final closure statement and the conditions permitting reopening.

questions.text: Which workflow statuses can the case hold and which transitions are permitted?
Which preconditions must be satisfied before the case may be closed?
What closure outcome is recorded, such as resolved, unresolved, transferred or withdrawn?
Under what conditions is a closed case reopened rather than a new case being opened?

data_elements.name: Case status
data_elements.description: Current workflow status of the response case.

data_elements.name: Closure outcome
data_elements.description: Recorded outcome at closure.

data_elements.name: Closure time
data_elements.description: Time the case was closed.

data_elements.name: Reopen reference
data_elements.description: Reference to the decision that reopened a previously closed case.

artifacts.name: Case closure statement
artifacts.description: Final statement of what was handled, what was done, what remains open and on what basis the case was closed.
artifacts.identity_strategy: Bound to the case identifier with a version marker so that corrections supersede rather than replace; no date component in the identifier.

findings.name: Post-incident review and improvement actions
findings.description: The structured review of the engagement and the improvement actions it generates, each with an owner, target and verification of implementation.

questions.text: Which review was held, who participated, and what scope was agreed?
Which findings concern the response process rather than the underlying technical cause?
Who owns each improvement action and by when must it be completed?
How is it verified that an improvement action was actually implemented and effective?
Which artefacts, such as playbooks, detection rules or the charter, must be updated as a result?

data_elements.name: Review finding
data_elements.description: A stated finding about the response process with its category.

data_elements.name: Improvement action
data_elements.description: Action with owner, target time and current status.

data_elements.name: Improvement verification
data_elements.description: Evidence that an improvement action was implemented and assessed.

artifacts.name: Post-incident review report
artifacts.description: Record of the review, its participants, findings and agreed decisions about the response process.
artifacts.identity_strategy: Bound to the case identifier with a version marker; where several reviews occur, each is distinguished by review type and participant set rather than by date.

artifacts.name: Improvement action register
artifacts.description: Register of actions arising from the review with owners, targets, status and verification references.
artifacts.identity_strategy: Master work-management identifier where one exists, otherwise a monotonic sequence in the improvement register namespace, cross-referenced to the originating case.

layers.name: Assurance and Measurement
layers.description: How response performance is measured and how the case record itself is validated.

findings.name: Response performance measurement
findings.description: Defined measures of response performance derived from typed case timestamps, with explicit definitions, windows and known data-quality limits.

questions.text: How is each response measure defined, including which timestamps bound it?
Which population of cases does a reported figure cover and over which window?
Which known data-quality limits would make a measure misleading?
Which decisions may and may not be based on these measures?

data_elements.name: Measure definition
data_elements.description: Named measure with its bounding timestamp types and unit.

data_elements.name: Measure value
data_elements.description: Computed value for a case or a case population.

data_elements.name: Measure caveat
data_elements.description: Known limitation affecting interpretation of a value.

findings.inline_only_rationale: Measures are derived values computed from typed timestamps already held on the case record; materialising them as a separate artifact would create a second, drifting source of truth, so they are kept as inline definitions and computed values.

findings.name: Case record validation and conformance claims
findings.description: Completeness and consistency rules the case record must satisfy at each state gate, and how alignment to external standards is claimed with evidence rather than asserted.

questions.text: Which fields must be present before the case may move to a given status?
Which cross-field consistency rules apply, such as recovery time not preceding detection time?
What evidence supports any claim of conformance to an external standard or profile?
answer_data: Scope and limits of the claim

questions.text: Which validation applies when the case is exported to an exchange format, and what is lost?

data_elements.name: Validation rule
data_elements.description: Rule that the case record must satisfy at a defined state gate.

data_elements.name: Validation result
data_elements.description: Outcome of applying validation rules to the case record.

data_elements.name: Alignment claim
data_elements.description: Declared alignment to an external standard with its supporting evidence and stated limits.

findings.inline_only_rationale: Validation rules and alignment claims are metadata about the case record rather than deliverables of the engagement; they are evaluated by the adopting platform against the inline record, and no separate transmissible object is produced by this model.

functions.name: Open response case
functions.description: Create a case aggregate for a declared or suspected incident, assign identity and bind the responding capability.
outputs: Response case record with case identifier
preconditions: Responding capability charter is published and current
Incident record reference resolves in the composing incident model
effects: Case identifier reserved in the issuing namespace
Case placed in an open status with a generation time recorded

functions.name: Record detection and report intake
functions.description: Register how the situation was discovered or reported, authenticate the reporter and acknowledge receipt.
preconditions: An open case exists or is created by this call
effects: Intake provenance attached to the case
Completeness assessment recorded for follow-up

functions.name: Declare incident and assign response tier
functions.description: Record the declaration decision and the triage outcome, including criteria version and started clocks.
preconditions: Declaring role holds the delegated authority recorded in the charter
effects: Case status transitions to an active response state
Response clocks begin from the recorded start times

functions.name: Bind governing playbook or procedure
functions.description: Attach the identity, version, validity window and integrity value of the externally governed playbook, or record ad hoc response.
outputs: Ad hoc response flag where applicable
preconditions: Playbook validity window covers the current time or a deviation is recorded
effects: Case records which procedure governs it without copying or executing that procedure

functions.name: Authorise response action
functions.description: Record an authorised containment, eradication or mitigation action with target, approver, intended effect and reversibility.
preconditions: Approver holds the decision right for the action class
Evidence preservation conflict has been assessed
effects: Action is authorised and tracked in the case; execution remains with the external system that performs it

functions.name: Attach execution evidence reference
functions.description: Link an authorised action to the executing system's record that it was performed, without importing execution or audit semantics.
outputs: Updated action record with outcome reference
preconditions: Action record exists and is in an authorised state
effects: Case can evidence that an action was carried out while the executing system remains the authority for how

functions.name: Request continuity or recovery plan invocation
functions.description: Emit a referenced invocation request with case-specific parameters to the model that owns the plan, and record the acknowledgement.
preconditions: Requesting role is authorised to invoke
Plan reference resolves in the referenced continuity and recovery model
effects: Invocation request and acknowledgement recorded on the case; plan activation state and execution remain owned by the referenced model

functions.name: Register evidence and record custody handoff
functions.description: Add an evidence item to the case register with integrity value and custodian, and record transfers at the case boundary.
preconditions: Acquisition was performed under the applicable handling constraints
effects: Case can demonstrate what it relied on and who held it; examination methodology stays with the forensic discipline

functions.name: Apply or release preservation hold
functions.description: Set or lift a hold that suspends routine disposal of case records and registered evidence, naming the authority and the executing party.
preconditions: A retention class is assigned to the case record
effects: Disposal is suspended or resumed; physical disposal is executed by the party named in the adopting Dimension's records policy

functions.name: Bind determined reporting obligation
functions.description: Attach an externally determined reporting regime to the case, derive stage deadlines from the recorded awareness time and track submissions.
preconditions: Awareness time is determined and recorded
Applicability was determined by the competent party outside this model
effects: Case carries computable deadlines and stage state without asserting the legal determination itself

functions.name: Record notification submission
functions.description: Retain the dispatched notification for a stage, its recipient authority, transmission facts and returned reference or delay justification.
preconditions: A regime binding exists for the stage being submitted
effects: Stage marked as submitted; missed deadlines carry a recorded justification

functions.name: Produce marked disclosure package
functions.description: Assemble case-derived material for a named recipient, apply the handling label to the material and record redactions and conditions.
preconditions: Handling label is set and the approving role has authorised the recipient class
effects: Onward sharing is traceable and conditions travel with the material

functions.name: Validate case record against state gate
functions.description: Evaluate completeness and cross-field consistency rules for a target status and report violations.
preconditions: Rule set for the target status is available
effects: Blocking violations prevent a status transition until remediated

functions.name: Close case and issue closure statement
functions.description: Verify closure preconditions, record the closure outcome and issue the final statement of handling.
preconditions: Restoration verification recorded or explicit exception approved
All blocking validation violations cleared
effects: Case status becomes closed; reopening requires a recorded decision

functions.name: Record post-incident review and improvement actions
functions.description: Capture review findings about the response process and open owned improvement actions with verification requirements.
preconditions: Case is closed or a review is scheduled for a long-running case
effects: Improvement actions are owned and tracked to verified implementation

functions.name: Compute response performance measures
functions.description: Derive defined measures from typed case timestamps for a stated case population and window, with caveats attached.
preconditions: Required timestamp types are present and typed
effects: Comparable measures produced without creating a second source of truth

functions.name: Export case to exchange format
functions.description: Project the case record into an external exchange representation, applying marking mappings and reporting information loss.
preconditions: Handling label maps to a supported marking in the target format or an unmapped-case note is produced
effects: Interchange is possible while divergences between vocabularies are recorded rather than hidden

composition.purpose: This model is registered as a child of WM-ACT-019 and specialises it for incident response only; generic activity, case and work-record scaffolding defined by the parent is inherited rather than restated here.

Incoming composition: a cyber incident is handled by a response case. WM-ACT-020 owns incident identity, category, severity, affected assets and impact facts; this model carries only references to them plus response-side decisions such as declaration, tier and clocks.

Outgoing reference: the response may request invocation of a continuity or recovery plan. This model carries the plan reference, trigger, invocation parameters and acknowledgement reference only; plan authoring, approval, testing, activation state and execution remain with WM-ACT-043.

composition.target: Candidate sibling model: digital forensics and evidence examination (not yet registered)
composition.purpose: Acquisition, examination, analysis methodology and expert reporting are referenced from the case rather than modelled here; this model retains only register entries, integrity values and custody handoffs at the case boundary.

composition.target: Candidate sibling model: regulatory obligation and jurisdiction register (not yet registered)
composition.purpose: Determination of which reporting regime and threshold applies is a legal determination owned elsewhere; this model binds the determined obligation to the case and records submissions and acknowledgements.

Alignment for case exchange: identifiers, typed times, discovery source, assessment, contact, expectation and history structures. Alignment is asserted at element level with recorded divergences and is not a conformance claim.
Alignment for playbook identity, versioning and validity when binding a governing procedure to a case; workflow execution, agents and targets remain outside this model.
Alignment for object identity, creation and modification markers, confidence, external references, notes and data markings when case content is exchanged as threat intelligence.
Handling and disclosure labels are applied as a cross-cutting marking vocabulary to case content and issued artifacts, with placement rules taken from the source specification.
External classification vocabulary bound by coded value and taxonomy version for interoperability with CSIRT and law-enforcement reporting; the vocabulary is not forked or maintained locally.

Alignment of case outcomes to cybersecurity risk-management outcomes so that response records can evidence detection, response, recovery and improvement expectations; conformance is claimed only with evidence.
Technique references are carried with an explicit catalogue version so that assertions remain resolvable across catalogue releases; technique definitions are not reproduced.

owner_package_requirements: The adopting Dimension must designate a single accountable owner for this model and a named response case owner role for each open case, with documented delegation when unavailable.

The owner package must declare the bindings this model leaves open: the incident model instance, the continuity and recovery model instance, the applicable reporting-regime register, the evidence discipline and the records retention policy.
The owner package must publish the responding capability's service description and keep the authority level, constituency and level of support current, since case decisions cite it.
The owner package must state which platform executes response actions and holds their audit trail, confirming that this model records authorisations and references only.
dimension.namespace_guidance: Use a stable dimension-scoped namespace of the form <dimension>.act.inc for case identifiers, with sub-namespaces per responding capability so that identifiers issued by cooperating teams remain distinguishable and can be carried as alternative identifiers. Namespaces must not encode dates, org-chart names or tool names that change on reorganisation or migration.
registry_links: Vercy registry entry vr.wm-act-042 with nav path NAV.ACT.INC and domain tag ACT.INC
Relation ledger entry composing WM-ACT-020 into this model and referencing WM-ACT-043
Adopting-Dimension register of responding capabilities, reporting regimes and evidence custodians

canonicalization_rules: Timestamps are canonicalised to RFC 3339 with seconds and an explicit offset or Z; the original local representation is retained as provenance where it carries meaning.
Identifiers are canonicalised as namespace plus local identifier; alternative identifiers held by other parties are kept as a separate typed collection and never overwrite the master identifier.
Coded values from external vocabularies are stored as the pairing of value and catalogue version; unmapped values are retained verbatim with an explicit unmapped marker rather than being coerced.
Free text is stored without presentational markup; handling labels are stored as structured values and rendered onto issued material at export.
patch_rules: Patches are additive: superseded values are retained with the superseding change entry, its author and its stated reason, because response records are reviewed after the fact.
Any change to a typed timestamp, declaration state, closure outcome or handling label requires a recorded reason and the acting role reference.
Correcting an issued artifact creates a superseding version referencing the prior identifier; issued notifications and disclosures are never edited in place.
Patches to a case under preservation hold are permitted only as additive corrections and must reference the hold notice.
compatibility_rules: Adding an optional data element, coded value or artifact type is a compatible change; making an element required, narrowing cardinality or removing a status value is breaking.
Changing the meaning of a typed timestamp, of the awareness time, or of a closure outcome is breaking even when the field name is unchanged.
External vocabulary version upgrades are compatible only when accompanied by a mapping and a revalidation record; unmapped values must be reported, not silently dropped.
Projections to exchange formats must declare known information loss; loss discovered later is treated as a defect against the projection, not against the model.

identity_priority: Identifier issued by the authoritative master system for the record, such as the case-management, work-management or evidence-management system of record in the adopting Dimension

Governed global identifier or IRI where the record is published under a registry or exchange-format namespace, including identifiers assigned by a cooperating authority and carried as alternative identifiers
UUID or ULID minted by the adopting Dimension when no master-system or governed identifier exists, recorded together with the minting namespace
artifact_rules.timestamp_rule: All time values use RFC 3339 with seconds and an explicit numeric offset or Z; local wall-clock strings without an offset are rejected. Event time, detection time, report time, containment time, recovery time and closure time are stored as separate typed values and must never be collapsed into one field, and the record generation or ingestion time is stored separately from every event time so that late or corrected reporting is visible. Where the two differ, both the event time and the observation or ingestion time are retained, with estimated times explicitly flagged and carrying an uncertainty interval.
artifact_rules.serial_naming_rule: Serial artifacts are numbered monotonically within an explicitly named parent namespace, normally the case identifier, starting at one and never reused, even after withdrawal. Serial numbers must not embed dates, years, periods or organisational codes; effective periods and audiences are carried as fields. Corrections take a new serial that references the superseded identifier.
artifact_rules.integrity_rule: Every issued artifact records a content digest with its named algorithm, the issuing role reference and the issue time; evidence register entries additionally record the digest captured at acquisition and each reverification. Integrity values are recorded and compared by this model, while the storage platform and the evidence discipline remain responsible for enforcing immutability and for the platform audit trail.

policies: Boundary policy: the case record cites incident facts, plan content, execution results and audit records by reference; it never copies or restates content that another model or system masters.
Authority policy: no containment, notification or disclosure entry is valid without a recorded acting role and the authority basis under which the role acted.
Handling policy: every case and every issued artifact carries a handling label, and onward disclosure is recorded with recipient, condition and any redaction.

Deadline policy: notification deadlines are computed from the recorded awareness time and the bound regime; a missed deadline is recorded with a reasoned justification rather than being retro-adjusted.
Falsifiability policy: hypotheses, estimates and confidence values are recorded as such and are distinguishable from observed facts at every point in the case record.

read: Reading a case record requires an assigned case role or an explicit grant; the handling label constrains what may be read and by whom.
Aggregated and de-identified reads for measurement are permitted without case-level grants where the population is large enough to prevent re-identification.
Every read of evidence register entries and of affected-party content is restricted to roles named in the case, with the reason for access recorded.
Historic versions and superseded values are readable to roles with review authority so that decisions can be reconstructed.
create: A case may be created only with a resolvable incident reference or an intake record, and always with an issued case identifier from the governed namespace.
Artifacts are created only by roles holding the corresponding decision right; issued notifications additionally require the recorded approval.
Every created record carries a generation time, a creating role reference and, where imported, a source system reference and ingestion time.
Duplicate detection runs on creation against open cases and alternative identifiers to prevent parallel handling of the same engagement.
update: Updates are additive and versioned; the superseded value, the acting role and the stated reason are retained.
Status transitions are permitted only where the target state's validation gate passes or an approved exception is recorded.
Handling labels may be relaxed only by the labelling authority or the original source, and the change is recorded with justification.
Issued artifacts are never updated in place; a superseding version is issued that references the prior identifier.
delete: Case records are not hard-deleted while a preservation hold is in force; the hold flag blocks all disposition until released by the recorded authority.

On release of a hold and expiry of the assigned retention class, disposition is applied to the case record and its attachments, and a tombstone is retained carrying the case identifier, retention class, disposition authority, disposition time and a statement of what was disposed, so that references from other models continue to resolve.

Erasure requests affecting personal data inside a case record are handled by minimising or redacting the affected elements while retaining the case skeleton and the breach documentation required of the controller; the request itself is adjudicated by the privacy or legal function, not by this model.

Execution of physical deletion, media sanitisation and backup expiry is owned by the adopting Dimension's records and platform policy; evidence disposal is owned by the evidence custodian and, where an evidence item is under legal control, by the competent authority. This model records the disposition decision and the tombstone but does not perform or enforce deletion.
Deletion of an artifact never deletes the references held by other models; broken references are reported as defects and resolved through the tombstone.

roles.name: Model steward
responsibilities: Maintain the model, its bindings and its alignment mappings, and record divergences from external standards
Approve compatible and breaking changes and publish the migration guidance

roles.name: Response case owner
responsibilities: Own an individual case end to end, including triage, decisions, escalation and closure
Ensure every decision carries an acting role and an authority basis
Request continuity or recovery plan invocation without assuming ownership of plan execution

roles.name: Records and disclosure controller
responsibilities: Assign retention classes, impose and release preservation holds and approve dispositions
Approve handling labels, recipients and redactions for onward disclosure

roles.name: Notification coordinator
responsibilities: Bind determined reporting obligations to the case and monitor stage deadlines
Retain submissions, acknowledgements and any reasoned justification for delay

roles.name: Interoperability maintainer
responsibilities: Maintain mappings to exchange formats and external vocabularies with their catalogue versions
Report information loss and unmapped values on export rather than silently coercing them

roles.name: Post-incident reviewer
responsibilities: Convene reviews, record findings about the response process and open owned improvement actions
Verify that improvement actions were implemented and assess whether they were effective

access.default_rule: Deny by default. Access is granted to roles assigned on the specific case, bounded further by the handling label carried by the content, and every grant is time-bounded and recorded with its reason.
exceptions: Break-glass access for a declared crisis, granted by a named authority, time-bounded and reviewed after closure
Regulator, supervisory authority or law-enforcement access under a recorded legal basis, which may override the handling label but is recorded as a disclosure entry
Legal counsel and privacy function access to affected-party content and evidence for obligation assessment
Aggregated and de-identified access for measurement and improvement reporting
Emergency read for a downstream continuity function limited to the invocation parameters it needs, not to the whole case
audit_requirements: The adopting Dimension's platform must log every read, grant, export and disposition of case content with actor, time, scope and reason, and must retain those logs at least as long as the case retention class.
Break-glass and authority-override accesses must be reviewed after case closure by a role independent of the case owner.

This model records references to such logs and the disclosure entries it creates; the semantics, integrity and retention of the platform audit trail are owned by the platform and the adopting Dimension's audit policy, not by this model.

read_order: Read AGENTS.md first and resolve Name, Type and the four URLs before touching any record
Read the specification to establish scope, boundaries and the out-of-scope list, especially incident facts, plan execution and action enforcement
Read the storage type description to learn how bundles, layers, findings and artifacts are projected in this deployment
Read the interface description for the read, create, update and delete operations available and their authorisation model
Read the processes description for state gates, validation rules, deadline handling and disposition
Resolve the bound sibling models and registers before opening or modifying a case

coverage.claim: Single-provider (Claude) coverage of the incident-response case surface: mandate and readiness binding, case identity and triage, detection intake and analysis, action authorisation and recovery coordination, evidence and chronology, notification and disclosure control, and closure, learning and measurement — 7 bundles, 15 layers, 26 findings, 108 questions, 18 artifacts and 17 functions grounded in 16 primary and 1 tier-3 secondary source. Coverage is claimed only for the response process, not for incident facts (WM-ACT-020), continuity-plan lifecycle (WM-ACT-043), action execution or audit-trail semantics. It is not complete for sector or national reporting regimes beyond NIS2 and GDPR, for non-cyber, OT and safety-of-life incident command, or for access-control and disposition-tombstone rules asserted in the coverage checklist but not carried by any finding. No independent second-provider review exists, so this is a reviewable draft, not a validated model.

checklist.notes: Case identifier plus alternative identifiers held by cooperating parties, with master-system identifier first in the identity priority and no date components permitted.
Declaration, triage, active response, restoration verification, closure and reopening are modelled as explicit states with gates; the incident's own lifecycle stays with WM-ACT-020.
Composition to the incident model, reference to continuity and recovery plans, related-activity links and alignments to external vocabularies are all typed and cited.

Event, detection, report, containment, recovery, closure and generation or ingestion times are separately typed in RFC 3339 with offsets; awareness time is singled out as the notification clock start.
Discovery source, reporting party, change history with author and reason, and source system plus ingestion time for imported elements.
Case owner, decision rights, handover records, residual risk acceptance and named disposition owner; plan and evidence ownership are explicitly external.
State-gate completeness rules, cross-field consistency rules, export validation with declared loss, and evidence-backed alignment claims rather than conformance assertions.
Deny-by-default with case-role grants bounded by handling labels, five named exception paths, and platform audit requirements stated as obligations on the adopting Dimension.

Retention class, preservation hold, tombstone on disposition, personal-data minimisation, and explicit statement that execution of deletion is owned by the records policy, evidence custodian or competent authority.
Alignments to IODEF, STIX, CACAO, TLP, RSIT and ATT&CK carry catalogue versions; unmapped values are retained with an explicit marker and loss is reported on export.
External taxonomy and technique bindings are carried by value and version; the response tier is modelled as a response-side decision distinct from incident severity.
